rationale: Second, independent scenario for unit-C-append-log-identity-consistency, keeping the same requirement and the already-accepted obligation. The plan exercises the other appendEntries early return: in a protocol-version-2 cluster a conflicting deprecated peer entry is stored successfully and then fails peer decoding, so the handler returns before setLastLog and the cached last log identity still names the index DeleteRange removed. The oracle is the follower's own acceptance of the leader's next valid AppendEntries for that range; construction in a scratch copy of the captured source showed cached_index 3 against stored_index 2 (consistent=false) and the follow-up request rejected because GetLog on the removed index fails. That local run is construction knowledge only - formal evidence requires the trusted runner's clean-copy execution, which is requested here. No defect is claimed until that execution and its correspondence review.
